subtitle: Interagency collaboration rests on a few basics. Learn to connect a shared purpose with each agency’s distinct contributions, clear terms, appropriate information and honest follow-through.
scope: For colleagues collaborating across agencies in work connected with DHS. Six original practice lessons use invented Agency A and Agency B and a proposed public-information explanation; they establish no actual agency mandate, eligibility process, service contact or sharing permission. Actual responsibilities, policy tools, appropriate information use and decision authority remain. Participation in this learning is voluntary. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Native American and Tribal-specific matters go to the appropriate office within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
introTranscript: Agencies can work toward a shared purpose while retaining different responsibilities. Follow two invented agencies through a complete flawed explanation, a task map and a terminology question. Receive two personally learned meanings of making a contribution clear, then examine an actual practice exchange and complete revised material. Compare ways to coordinate without merging authority or assuming information permission, and close with the exact gains and work still open. You can use the whole an example or keep an intrinsic insight privately without creating a real agency agreement.

lessons.title: Name the shared purpose without merging authority
lessons.summary: Read the complete explanation and locate the difference between coordinated information and another agency’s decision.
lessons.objective: Describe the whole practice explanation and its unsupported approval implication.
objectives: Describe the whole practice explanation and its unsupported approval implication.
Distinguish shared purpose from transferred agency authority.
Identify a useful reader task that both contributions could support.
takeaways: A common purpose can connect distinct responsibilities.
One agency’s draft state does not establish another agency’s decision.
A coordinated explanation should help a reader locate the actual task and its limits.
lessons.statement: Share a purpose without assuming one agency can decide another agency’s work.

image.caption: People sit along a long table with open laptops; one person stands at a whiteboard.

intro.heading: Read what the joint explanation promises
intro.body:
Em is a colleague proposing a joint information explanation with two invented public agencies. Suri at Agency A has a practice contribution role in drafting words about a request step. Reva at Agency B has a contribution role in drafting words about a review step. These are educational drafting responsibilities, not actual Minnesota mandates, contacts, eligibility rules or authority to decide a person’s services.

The whole original explanation is: “For help understanding a request, ask Agency A. Once Agency A says the explanation is complete, Agency B has approved the review and no question remains.” The first sentence offers an invented help role. The second transfers a draft status into another agency’s approval and then claims every question resolved. Nothing in the supplied contribution roles establishes that transfer or result.

A shared purpose could be to help a reader distinguish a question about the request explanation from a question about the review explanation. Both agencies could contribute without becoming one agency or giving a single person every authority. The reader task is to locate what kind of information is being offered and what remains to be clarified, not to obtain a practice approval through a course example.

GAO’s 2023 federal collaboration guidance describes common outcomes, roles, relevant participants and resources as connected practices. Its concepts can support inquiry into a cross-agency task; they do not establish a current DHS collaboration structure or import federal agency arrangements as Minnesota requirements. Em can ask what each contribution covers and how they connect, rather than assume a common logo or page title supplies those answers.

A useful start retains both the possible benefit and the authority boundary. Readers might benefit from explanations that connect rather than contradict each other. That benefit remains a proposal until actual contributions and relevant responses are supplied. Privately locate the second sentence’s unsupported implication, or reflect on a learned assumption that together means all decisions merged. Such intrinsic understanding requires no real case, public account or agency agreement.

inThisLesson: Read the two complete explanation sentences.
Locate the unsupported transfer and universal claim.
Keep contributions and actual authority distinct.
lessons.keyStatement: The supplied drafting roles can support connected information; Agency A’s explanation state establishes neither Agency B approval nor every question resolved.

flashcards.back: Work connecting contributions across agencies toward a shared purpose while their actual responsibilities and authority remain.
The issue collaborators want to address together, not proof every contribution or outcome is agreed.
A particular part someone can prepare or examine through actual responsibility, distinct from every decision related to it.
The limit of what a role may decide, which a shared page or planning note does not automatically change.
A word collaborators use with an explained meaning; the same word may otherwise hide different states.
Examining the actual contributions and next responsibilities rather than assume an agreement has completed the work.

accordion.heading: Make the common task and boundaries understandable

items.title: Connected information can serve a real question
items.body: A reader may need to distinguish the request and review explanations rather than navigate inconsistent words alone. That purpose gives the two drafting contributions a reason to connect. It does not establish the reader’s actual service needs, a working help route or an existing agency program.

items.title: A shared surface supplies no decision transfer
items.body: The explanation’s second sentence makes one draft state another agency’s approval. Nothing about sharing a page establishes that authority. Clarifying who can contribute to wording and who can make an actual decision prevents the explanation from promising a result it cannot support.

items.title: A purpose statement is a beginning rather than completion
items.body: Em can propose a useful reader question and seek the relevant contributions. No task acceptance, actual resources or publication decision is supplied yet. A good purpose can guide the next inquiry without becoming evidence that the joint work exists or every agency requirement has been met.

tabs.label: Together means every authority is merged
tabs.body: This frame enlarges a shared explanation into a single decision power. It hides the different contribution roles and the unsupported second sentence. The course grants no mandate transfer, actual service decision or universal question-resolution guarantee.

tabs.label: Distinct roles mean collaboration cannot help
tabs.body: This frame would discard the possible benefit of connecting request and review explanations. Separate responsibilities can be made understandable while information is coordinated. A boundary on decisions does not itself prevent a useful contribution or shared purpose.

tabs.label: Connect the reader purpose and distinct contributions
tabs.body: This frame gives the task a concrete question while preserving what each role can and cannot supply. It allows a map and terminology discussion to develop without making the shared page its own approval process. The actual result remains to be examined.

check.question: What does the supplied beginning establish?
check.correct: Two invented drafting roles and a possible shared reader purpose, with an explanation that wrongly turns one agency’s draft state into another agency’s approval and every question resolved.
wrong: Agency A’s completed draft automatically approves Agency B’s review.
A shared explanation gives Em every actual agency mandate.
Distinct agency responsibilities make any connected information impossible.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The beginning gives a useful collaboration question and a precise unsupported promise to examine.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A draft state is not another agency’s approval. A shared explanation grants no actual mandate to Em. Distinct responsibilities can still support connected information; retain the possible reader benefit while clarifying the exact contribution and decision boundaries.

sorting.heading: Separate supplied contribution, shared inquiry and unsupported transfer

items.text: Suri’s practice role concerns request-explanation words.
Reva’s practice role concerns review-explanation words.
How could a reader distinguish the two explanation questions?
Which actual decisions are outside these drafting contributions?
Agency A’s draft status approves all Agency B decisions.
A joint page proves no questions remain.

move.control: You can connect a shared purpose with actual distinct contributions.
move.failure: Joint work becomes merged authority or an assumed universal outcome.

lessons.title: Map contributions and clarify shared terms
lessons.summary: Develop a task map and examine how the word complete can hide different states.
lessons.objective: Describe the proposed three-role map and its unaccepted state.
objectives: Describe the proposed three-role map and its unaccepted state.
Explain the different meanings the people describe of complete without inferring motives.
Develop clearer status language that does not imply approval.
takeaways: A task map can make handoffs visible without delegating authority.
Shared words need an explained context.
A proposed responsibility is not an accepted commitment.
lessons.statement: Say what the task and status mean before relying on a shared word to connect the work.

image.caption: People sit along a long table with open laptops; one person stands at a whiteboard.

intro.heading: Make the handoff and status visible
intro.body:
Em proposes this complete task map in ordinary sentences: “Suri would draft the request explanation within Agency A’s contribution. Reva would draft the review explanation within Agency B’s contribution. Em would connect the two passages and ask each colleague whether the combined words represent the contribution accurately. Actual decisions, appropriate material, acceptance, capacity and publication arrangements would still need their own basis.” The map is proposed, not an actual delegation or accepted work agreement.

The word complete also needs attention. Suri says: “For this draft, I meant that the two requested request-explanation sentences are present.” Reva says: “For my contribution, I would mean ready for my wording review, not approved review results.” These are particular explanations of a word in the example, not evidence of a national culture or a permanent organizational trait. Neither person has said an actual application, review or service decision is complete.

A clearer status could be request-explanation sentences present or review explanation ready for wording examination, with the person and material attached. That is more informative than complete on its own. It still does not prove the words accurate, the contribution accepted or the reader helped. A task map can reveal the point where one role’s output informs another’s work without making it automatic sign-off.

GAO’s guidance discusses common terminology and agreed roles as useful collaboration considerations. Here those concepts are applied through the whole map and exact status explanations. The course establishes no mandatory map template, approval ladder or deadline. An actual project would need relevant roles and authority, including whether its proposed way of sharing material is appropriate. A map with every box filled is not by itself evidence that those conditions have been settled.

Privately locate the handoff and status distinctions. You may also recognize how an ordinary familiar word can sound final while meaning different things to different people. That insight can support better questions without demanding that another person explain cultural affiliations or labeling an agency inefficient. The next lesson adds a separate meaning encounter rather than assuming these technical status explanations reveal the collaborators’ personal cultures.

inThisLesson: Read Suri’s and Reva’s exact status meanings.
lessons.keyStatement: The map and exact meanings make contributions more understandable; proposed tasks and clearer status words establish no acceptance, approved result or decision transfer.

accordion.heading: Keep the task and word attached to their context

items.title: The proposed map reveals a connection and open conditions
items.body: Suri and Reva would prepare different passages, while Em would compare the combined words with their contributions. The final sentence keeps actual decisions and arrangements open. That prevents a task list from becoming a hidden authority transfer or evidence of accepted capacity.

items.title: The same word can name different material states
items.body: Suri’s complete concerns sentences present; Reva’s concerns readiness for a wording review. Neither means actual review results approved. A question about the object and scope of a status is more useful than assuming the other colleague is being evasive or the agencies share one meaning automatically.

items.title: A clearer label remains evidence at a limited scope
items.body: Request-explanation sentences present identifies a specific state. It supplies no reader feedback, accuracy finding or publication decision. Clear terminology helps coordinate without settling facts that the terminology does not contain; the underlying work needs its own relevant evidence and roles.

tabs.heading: Compare ways to handle a handoff

tabs.label: Use complete as universal sign-off
tabs.body: This approach keeps the ambiguity and repeats the initial explanation’s authority problem. One material state becomes an approved result for another agency. It could encourage a next step with no actual basis; ask what is complete and what the statement permits.

tabs.label: Build a detailed map and call all tasks accepted
tabs.body: A longer map may reveal proposed responsibilities, but it does not show each person can take them or actual authority allows the arrangement. The map’s value is in making those questions visible, rather than turning administrative detail into an operational agreement.

tabs.label: Map the contribution and name its actual status
tabs.body: This approach shows the proposed passages, connection and limited status words. It lets colleagues examine an actual handoff with acceptance and approval still separate. It is a useful planning practice rather than a universal agency method or guaranteed resolution.

check.question: Which account fits the complete map and status explanations?
check.correct: The proposed passages and connection are understandable, and complete has two material-specific meanings; actual acceptance, accuracy, authority and approval remain unestablished.
wrong: A completed task map means both agencies accepted every task.
Suri’s sentences-present status proves Agency B review approval.
The different status meanings prove a permanent cultural deficiency in one agency.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The map and explained words support clearer coordination without enlarging their evidence or authority.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A proposed map is not task acceptance. Sentences present is not another agency’s approved result. Different contextual word meanings do not establish a cultural deficiency; clarify the material state and keep practical and decision conditions distinct.

sorting.heading: Separate proposed contribution, supplied status meaning and unsupported result

items.text: Suri would draft the request explanation.
Em would connect the passages and ask about accurate representation.
Suri means the requested sentences are present.
Reva means ready for a wording review, not approved results.
The map proves accepted staff time and publication permission.
Complete always means every agency decision approved.

This makes the handoff useful without inventing commitments or power.

lessons.transfer: Privately explain a material-specific status and its limit, or reflect on how a familiar word can conceal different meanings without a real task map.

move.control: You can attach status words to material, role and scope before relying on them.
move.failure: A map or shared word becomes accepted work, universal approval or an agency profile.

lessons.title: Receive meanings of a clear contribution
lessons.summary: Widen judgments through two chosen learned meanings and change a voluntary invitation.
lessons.objective: Explain Mira’s and Teo’s personally learned meanings of naming a contribution.
objectives: Explain Mira’s and Teo’s personally learned meanings of naming a contribution.
Describe how their accounts widen Arden’s narrow judgments.
Develop a concrete contextual invitation without predicting agency behavior or compelling acceptance.
takeaways: A request for a named piece can carry recognition or responsibility.
A chosen explanation can widen a frame without becoming a group script.
The changed offer should follow the actual meanings and preserve choice.
lessons.statement: Understand what making a contribution clear means to the person before judging it as control or a wish for credit.

image.caption: People sit along a long table with open laptops; one person stands at a whiteboard.

intro.heading: Look beyond a first judgment of the request
intro.body:
A separate voluntary local-history display provides another conversation to explore. Arden invites Mira and Teo to help explain an everyday object. Mira asks which named part could be attributed to her; Teo asks which part he would be responsible to check. Arden initially hears Mira as seeking status and Teo as trying to control the shared account. Neither has accepted a contribution or explained the request yet.

Mira chooses to explain that in a small radio story circle, naming a contribution made the work recognizable: a person could know whose chosen words were being used rather than have a complete story assigned to a crowd. It was a way to preserve authorship, not a demand for superiority. Teo chooses to explain that in a bicycle-building circle, naming the joint he would check meant others could rely on a particular responsibility without assuming he had examined the whole bicycle. The boundary protected the shared work rather than giving him control over every contribution.

Those personally learned purposes widen Arden’s status and control judgments. A named contribution can make authorship visible, and a bounded check can make responsibility dependable. Neither account demonstrates a permanent trait, a rule about all radio or bicycle communities, or an agency’s motives. These meanings do not explain Suri’s or Reva’s word use by prediction; their particular status explanations remain their own.

Arden changes the invitation to these full four sentences: “The proposed display would distinguish a chosen object account from what we have not examined. You could offer a sentence you are willing to have considered with its contribution named, or identify a particular detail you would consider checking. We would keep that selected contribution distinct from permission to retell a whole history or a check of the entire object. Would one of those forms fit, or would you prefer a different question?” The invitation gives an identifiable contribution and limit rather than simply asking people to stop wanting control or credit.

The changed offer follows received meanings while acceptance, accurate attribution, actual checking and display arrangements remain open. It creates no authority over an actual agency record or a real person’s story. Privately compare the first judgments with the two meanings and proposed words. You can retain an intrinsic insight about authorship or dependable boundaries without disclosing your history or making a public contribution.

inThisLesson: Keep agency motives and acceptance separate.
lessons.keyStatement: Mira’s recognizable authorship and Teo’s dependable bounded check widen Arden’s frame and change the full offer, without establishing a group style or accepted contribution.

accordion.heading: Connect the offered meaning with the response

items.title: Named authorship need not be status competition
items.body: Mira’s radio-circle account concerns knowing whose words are considered. It helps Arden hear an authorship purpose rather than only a demand to be more important. That purpose can remain meaningful without giving Mira permission to speak for a community or predicting all attribution preferences.

items.title: A bounded check can protect shared responsibility
items.body: Teo’s bicycle account explains why naming one checked joint prevented a larger assurance. Arden can now hear the limit as dependable responsibility rather than control over everything. It supplies no actual check result or guarantee the object is safe, and it should not be used as an analogy to make technical safety findings in agency work.

items.title: The offer changes through both meanings
items.body: The full invitation names the selected sentence or detail, distinguishes them from whole-story permission and whole-object examination, and asks what fits. It receives the purposes rather than renaming the original judgments. Choice, actual contribution and arrangements remain open; meaningful interpretation change does not prove those later outcomes.

tabs.label: Treat named contributions as ego or control
tabs.body: This frame makes Arden’s initial judgment the final explanation even after two different purposes are supplied. It could hide authorship and dependable responsibility under one negative label. The accounts provide a reason to widen the frame without declaring every request for credit or a boundary appropriate in every setting.

tabs.label: Turn the accounts into agency profiles
tabs.body: This frame would predict Suri and Reva from unrelated chosen communities. Mira and Teo have given particular personal meanings, not a census, instrument or explanation of government behavior. The actual partners’ words and responsibilities still need their own account.

tabs.label: Offer selected contribution and a clear limit
tabs.body: This frame follows recognizable authorship and bounded checking into Arden’s complete invitation. It preserves a concrete task and freedom to choose a different question. Its gain is a meaning-informed proposal, with attribution, checking and arrangements still unperformed.

check.question: Which account follows the actual meanings?
check.correct: Mira’s and Teo’s chosen purposes widen Arden’s judgments and inform a full selected-contribution offer, while actual agency motives, acceptance and work results remain open.
wrong: Mira’s named-contribution request proves she values status above the shared work.
Teo’s bicycle account predicts all Agency B responsibilities and motives.
Arden’s changed invitation proves every story permission and check is complete.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The encounter connects meaning and response while preserving choice and the actual scope of each account.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Mira offers an authorship purpose rather than evidence of status superiority. Teo’s personal account predicts no agency. A changed invitation completes neither checking nor story permission; retain the widened interpretation and proposed choice without manufacturing later results.

sorting.heading: Separate received meaning, changed offer and unsupported prediction

items.text: Mira connects named contributions with recognizable authorship.
Teo connects a bounded check with dependable shared responsibility.
Arden offers a selected sentence or particular detail with its limit.
Arden asks whether a different question would fit.
Every radio-circle participant prioritizes status.
Reva’s agency motives are proved by Teo’s chosen account.

scenario.prompt: What follows from the two meanings?
options: Profile the agencies from the chosen communities.
Require both people to accept because the offer changed.

responses: The personal accounts predict no government role or motive.
Hearing a purpose does not compel this voluntary contribution.
This connects real meaning learning with a concrete proposal without enlarging its result.

lessons.transfer: Privately examine how a named contribution can protect authorship or responsibility, or retain an intrinsic insight without a real partner exchange or biography.

move.control: You can receive a chosen purpose and change an offer without classifying the person.
move.failure: A contribution boundary becomes a character verdict or an agency profile.

lessons.title: Read the contribution and clarify practical arrangements
lessons.summary: Develop a whole planning note from exact partner responses without assuming resources or information permission.
lessons.objective: Describe Suri’s and Reva’s complete responses at their actual scope.
objectives: Describe Suri’s and Reva’s complete responses at their actual scope.
Explain the proposed note’s contribution and practical questions.
Distinguish a planning record from actual accepted resources or lawful information use.
takeaways: Partners’ responses may supply different parts of the plan.
Useful documentation keeps commitments and open questions distinct.
An agreement does not automatically authorize information or every decision.
lessons.statement: Make the contribution and remaining conditions visible rather than letting a planning note stand for every arrangement.

image.caption: People sit along a long table with open laptops; one person stands at a whiteboard.

intro.heading: Read what each partner actually offers
intro.body:
Return to the agency fiction. Suri says: “I can prepare invented words describing the request-explanation contribution. I cannot make Agency B’s decisions from those words.” Reva says: “I can offer wording about what the review explanation covers. I do not have actual review criteria, decisions or reader needs in this material.” These are the complete responses. They identify possible content contributions and particular limits, not accepted publication arrangements or an actual agency service.

Em proposes this whole planning note: “Suri would prepare the request-explanation passage and Reva the review-explanation passage using this invented material. Em would connect the passages and ask both colleagues whether the combined words represent the offered contributions. The account would identify missing actual review criteria, decision roles and reader needs rather than invent them. Appropriate time, information arrangements, acceptance and publication responsibilities remain to be clarified.” The note makes the possible work understandable while retaining the unanswered practical conditions.

GAO’s federal guidance discusses resources and information arrangements alongside roles, and documentation where appropriate. It expressly does not make a formal agreement necessary for every collaboration. The practice note is an educational way to retain this plan’s scope, not a mandatory memorandum or proof an actual agency agreement exists. A signature, attractive format or completed field would not supply authority beyond the relevant responsibilities.

The material is invented, so no actual record is transferred here. In real collaboration, the question would include which information is relevant and which responsibilities govern its use and sharing. The course provides no legal permission to circulate a real case, staff details or service information. Replacing names with initials alone would not settle that question. A practice counterpart or appropriately available source can sometimes support a learning discussion while actual information arrangements are examined.

Resources are also still open: the responses do not supply a deadline, actual staffing commitment, budget or task priority. A possible contribution can be useful without guaranteeing its execution. Privately identify the two offers and one unanswered arrangement in the note. You may also reflect on a learned association between a written plan and certainty. The point is to retain the meaning of the plan without requiring a real memorandum or another person’s private information as learning proof.

inThisLesson: Locate actual missing criteria and arrangements.
Keep documentation distinct from permission and resources.
lessons.keyStatement: The partners offer possible wording contributions and the note preserves their scope; it supplies no actual information permission, accepted capacity or publication decision.

accordion.heading: Give the plan evidence rather than assumed certainty

items.title: Responses can make possible work more specific
items.body: Suri offers request-explanation words and Reva review-scope words. Each also names a limit. These responses give Em more than the initial task-map proposal, yet do not provide the actual criteria, reader needs or decision roles that a real page would require. Retain the offers and their unanswered parts together.

items.title: Documentation should preserve states rather than blur them
items.body: The proposed note describes contributions and explicitly leaves practical arrangements open. Calling it an approved agreement would overstate the record. Its educational value is to keep the plan inspectable for further discussion, not to grant every actor acceptance or authority through the document’s existence.

items.title: Information and capacity need their own basis
items.body: The invented words can be examined without actual records, but a real collaboration would need appropriate information and resource arrangements. A request or note does not settle them. Neither every-record sharing nor total avoidance is a useful automatic rule; ask what is relevant and permitted through actual responsibilities.

tabs.label: Treat the note as permission to share everything
tabs.body: This approach would enlarge educational documentation into information authority. The practice material includes no real records or sharing decision. A plan can identify the need for appropriate information without authorizing circulation of every record a colleague might find useful.

tabs.label: Treat offers as accepted deadlines and publication
tabs.body: This approach would turn can prepare and can offer into an actual timing and release commitment. The responses supply none of that. Practical conditions should be clarified rather than assuming a common purpose makes every requested resource available.

tabs.label: Retain exact offers and practical questions
tabs.body: This approach carries the two contribution scopes into the complete note with missing criteria, reader needs and arrangements visible. It makes further discussion more concrete while leaving resources and actual authority open. Documentation serves the work without becoming a guarantee or universal procedure.

check.question: Which account matches the responses and proposed note?
check.correct: Two possible content contributions and their limits are clearer, with actual criteria, reader needs, information arrangements, capacity and publication responsibilities still unestablished.
wrong: The note gives permission to share any real service record across agencies.
The offered contributions automatically accept a deadline and release commitment.
GAO makes a formal memorandum compulsory for every collaboration.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. A useful plan preserves the contributions and open conditions rather than granting them through its format.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A practice note grants no real-record sharing permission. Possible offers supply neither deadline nor release acceptance. GAO explicitly distinguishes appropriate documentation from a universal formal-agreement requirement; retain the plan’s actual scope and clarify its remaining conditions.

sorting.heading: Separate offered contribution, open condition and unsupported agreement

items.text: Suri can prepare invented request-explanation words.
Reva can offer wording about review-explanation scope.
Actual criteria, reader needs and decision roles.
Appropriate time, information use and publication responsibilities.
Every actual private record can be shared because a note exists.
Both partners accepted a universal deadline and final release.

lessons.title: Connect the contributions without creating a new approval process
lessons.summary: Compare three whole proposals and develop the explanation while retaining actual agency tools and decisions.
lessons.objective: Compare three complete coordination proposals and their consequences.
objectives: Compare three complete coordination proposals and their consequences.
Describe how the whole revised explanation addresses the unsupported transfer.
Preserve actual agency analysis and authority without making the consultant a universal gate.
takeaways: Coordination can connect explanations while roles remain distinct.
A revision should answer the unsupported implication at its source.
Actual tools and decisions need their own basis in real work.
lessons.statement: Connect what the partners can contribute without making the joint explanation a decision power of its own.

image.caption: People sit along a long table with open laptops; one person stands at a whiteboard.

intro.heading: Compare the whole next-step choices
intro.body:
Three complete proposals are supplied. A says: “Put both agency names on the page and let Agency A’s complete status approve every review decision.” B says: “Keep the passages entirely unrelated because agencies have different roles; do not explain how a reader’s questions connect.” C says: “Connect the offered explanation passages, describe their distinct scopes and unanswered practical questions, and seek actual sources, authority and appropriate arrangements before real use.” C preserves a possible coordination benefit without inventing an approval process.

The example then supplies a performed wording exchange. Suri says: “The request passage can tell a reader what kind of explanation I offer, not what Agency B decided.” Reva says: “The review passage can name its scope while saying criteria and actual decisions are not in this material.” These exact contributions help Em distinguish explanation and decision. They provide no actual service criteria, contact details or reader-tested route.

Em writes this complete replacement: “The proposed request explanation concerns how the request step is described. The proposed review explanation concerns how the review step is described. These drafting contributions do not establish an actual review decision, current help route or every reader’s needs. Sources, practical arrangements and actual decision responsibilities remain to be clarified before any real use.” The four sentences remove the automatic approval implication and universal no-question claim without promising that the invented material is an implemented service page.

Actual DHS Equity Policy keeps staff equity work and agency tools connected with real responsibilities. Under its qualifying prolonged or long-term action condition scheduled for the listed leadership approval, the actual formal analysis or scan within the agency toolkit, or a customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director, remains. A shared-page planning note and voluntary wording exercise do not replace that analysis or override another agency’s responsibilities. The consultant leads this program and supports capability; that guidance creates no gate requiring the consultant to approve every collaboration request.

Privately explain why C fits and how each replacement sentence responds to the original problem. You may also retain a meaningful insight about coordinating distinct perspectives without collapsing them into one. The course provides no permission to publish actual information, promise a help route or claim compliance from a well-formed practice note. The actual performed contributions can be useful while real-use conditions remain unfinished.

inThisLesson: Read the performed Suri/Reva wording exchange.
Preserve actual tools and decision roles.
lessons.keyStatement: Proposal C and the complete replacement connect offered explanations while removing automatic approval and universal resolution claims; real sources, arrangements and authority remain open.

accordion.heading: Keep coordination useful and authority honest

items.title: A repeats the unsupported transfer under a joint label
items.body: Both agency names would not make Suri’s draft state an actual review decision. A leaves the original reasoning problem untouched. A shared page can make contributions visible, but cannot authorize one agency to decide another’s work simply through branding or a common status word.

items.title: B discards a possible benefit of connection
items.body: Separate roles do not mean a reader must receive unrelated explanations. B would make the authority boundary a reason to avoid clarifying how questions differ and connect. A fitting relationship between passages can retain distinct responsibilities without turning them into a single approval chain.

items.title: C changes the words through the actual contribution
items.body: Suri and Reva distinguish their explanations from criteria and decisions not supplied. Em’s full replacement retains that distinction and identifies real-use questions. It is a performed wording change, not an approved procedure or substitute for actual analysis, evidence and authority.

tabs.label: A: Shared names create universal approval
tabs.body: This proposal would turn the joint surface into a decision mechanism without any actual basis. It retains the false completion-to-approval link. No course document, common label or contributor statement creates that agency authority or a universal resolved-question result.

tabs.label: B: Different roles prevent any connection
tabs.body: This proposal overlooks the shared reader purpose and the useful distinctions the partners can contribute. It would keep the authority boundary but discard coordination. Readers could still benefit from understanding different question scopes, even while actual services and decisions remain separate.

tabs.label: C: Connect offered scopes with real-use questions open
tabs.body: This proposal uses the complete contributions and replacement to make the distinct passages understandable. It keeps sources, criteria, practical arrangements and agency tools with actual responsibilities. The gain is a supported revision and next inquiry rather than publication, compliance or every reader’s usable access.

check.question: Which proposal fits the performed contribution and real responsibilities?
check.correct: C: connect the explanation scopes and remove unsupported approval and universal claims, while preserving actual sources, arrangements, policy tools and decision authority before real use.
wrong: A: using both names makes one agency’s draft status every agency’s approval.
B: distinct responsibilities make any connected explanation inappropriate.
A complete learning note automatically replaces all qualifying formal equity analysis.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. C keeps the possible reader benefit and actual responsibility boundaries together.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Shared names grant no decision transfer. Different responsibilities do not by themselves make connected information inappropriate. A learning note cannot substitute for the source policy’s actual qualifying analysis; use the precise contribution without inflating its authority or erasing its coordination value.

sorting.heading: Separate supported revision, actual-use question and unsupported substitute

items.text: The replacement describes the two offered explanation scopes separately.
It removes automatic approval and no-questions-remain claims.
Actual criteria, help routes and relevant reader needs.
Real sources, practical arrangements and decision responsibilities.
Both names merge all agency decision powers.
The optional note is every required formal analysis completed.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A merges decisions through names, B abandons connection, and C keeps scopes and real-use questions distinct. Suri/Reva actual wording contributions lead to Em’s complete four-sentence revision; no real-use approval is supplied.
scenario.prompt: Which way should the proposed work continue?
options: A, by treating names and complete status as all-agency approval.
C, by retaining the connected explanation and its scope while clarifying actual sources, arrangements and decisions.
B, by deciding different responsibilities make useful shared information impossible.
responses: The proposal supplies no authority or actual outcome.
This preserves the performed contribution and unfinished real-use conditions.
Separate roles can still support connected information.

lessons.transfer: Privately compare the three whole proposals and trace the replacement’s reason, or keep an intrinsic insight about shared work with distinct responsibility.

move.control: You can connect a contribution without inventing an approval process.
move.failure: A shared explanation merges powers or substitutes for real analysis, or separate roles erase every possible common purpose.

lessons.title: Follow through with gains and responsibilities intact
lessons.summary: Read the exact closing comments and distinguish a useful revision from an established interagency service outcome.
lessons.objective: Describe Suri’s and Reva’s complete closing comments at their actual scope.
objectives: Describe Suri’s and Reva’s complete closing comments at their actual scope.
Distinguish the revised explanation from implementation and broader reader outcomes.
Identify a fitting next inquiry or private learning without claiming a permanent partnership.
takeaways: A completed wording exchange is not a completed service arrangement.
Follow-through needs actual responsibilities rather than assumed continuity.
Particular coordination gains and intrinsic insight can matter while outcomes remain open.
lessons.statement: Recognize the contribution and keep unfinished responsibilities visible rather than making the closing a blanket success claim.

image.caption: People sit along a long table with open laptops; one person stands at a whiteboard.

intro.heading: Read the actual closing and continuation
intro.body:
Suri’s complete closing comment is: “The replacement no longer makes my draft state Agency B’s decision. It describes my contribution more accurately; actual help arrangements are not supplied.” Reva says: “My explanation scope is distinct from an approved result. Actual criteria and reader needs are still absent.” These are the complete supplied replies. They support particular judgments about the revision and open questions, not a formal agreement, service outcome or universal reader response.

Em’s whole closing account is: “The agencies’ possible contributions now connect without an automatic approval implication. The performed wording exchange and replacement are available to examine, with Suri and Reva identifying particular gains and unfinished information. Actual criteria, help arrangements, decision responsibilities, capacity, publication and reader experience remain open.” This account does not describe a real DHS partnership or completed information-sharing arrangement.

A fitting continuation would clarify the real-use question through relevant sources and actual roles if the proposal were taken forward. Someone would also need responsibility for examining whether the explanation remained accurate as conditions changed. The course supplies no accepted maintenance assignment, mandatory meeting cadence or deadline. GAO’s guidance discusses revisiting shared outcomes and appropriate agreements; those concepts support attention to continuity rather than a claim that the note guarantees it.

The learning gains are concrete. The first explanation falsely made one draft state another agency’s approval. The proposed task map and exact status meanings made the handoff more understandable. The performed contributions supported a complete revision, and the closing comments recognize their particular scope. The separate Mira/Teo encounter widened judgments through personally learned purposes and changed an invitation; it neither diagnosed agencies nor supplied an operational result.

Privately identify a gain and one unfinished responsibility using the example. You may instead retain an intrinsic insight about authorship, bounded contribution or the meaning of together, without creating an agreement or public note. There is no need to describe the partnership as permanently successful, certify cultural competence or obtain another person’s story to finish the learning. Staff continue their actual equity work with consultant program leadership and the course’s precise optional participation and training-credit exception.

inThisLesson: Value specific gains without certifying partnership success.
lessons.keyStatement: The closing supports more accurate contribution and decision distinctions, with actual arrangements, criteria, use and continuity still open; the example establishes no permanent agency partnership or reader outcome.

accordion.heading: Close with the actual contribution and next question

items.title: The two comments recognize different boundaries
items.body: Suri’s comment concerns the removed transfer from a draft state to Agency B’s decision and missing help arrangements. Reva’s concerns explanation versus approved result and absent criteria and needs. Each is meaningful without becoming a release decision, final agreement or evidence all readers can use the material.

items.title: Continuity needs actual responsibility and information
items.body: An explanation could become inaccurate if responsibilities or wording changed. A fitting plan would consider who examines that issue through actual authority, but the example accepts no maintenance task. A note or successful wording exchange alone guarantees no sustained collaboration or permitted future sharing.

items.title: Intrinsic learning can remain distinct from operational claims
items.body: Mira’s authorship and Teo’s bounded-check meaning can help you understand an invitation differently. That private growth does not depend on a real interagency project. It should not be reported as a service outcome, and its legitimacy need not be denied because no public artifact or accepted task follows.

tabs.label: Certify a permanent successful partnership
tabs.body: This account enlarges possible offers, wording contributions and limited comments into an established agency outcome. It would hide criteria, arrangements, actual reader experience and continuity not supplied. The example shows specific learning rather than a real operational partnership or permanent competence.

tabs.label: Erase gains because real use is unfinished
tabs.body: This account loses the actual map, status clarification, performed exchange and complete revision. Real-use questions remain, yet the particular contribution can be recognized. Unknown operational outcomes limit the claim rather than make all coordination or personal meaning learning worthless.

tabs.label: Retain gains and actual continuation questions
tabs.body: This account keeps exact comments and the reason for the replacement attached to the material. It allows a fitting next inquiry or private reflection without promising resources, assigning maintenance or inventing an approval. It closes honestly while leaving future work with actual responsibilities.

check.question: Which closing account fits the whole record?
check.correct: The task map, exact status meanings, performed contributions and complete revision support particular coordination gains, while actual real-use arrangements, decisions, reader experience and continuity remain open.
wrong: The replies prove a permanent partnership and every reader’s successful access.
The course note authorizes future sharing of all actual agency records.
Unfinished actual use means the performed revision and private insight have no value.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. This retains meaningful progress and the closing’s actual limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The replies concern particular wording and responsibility distinctions, not permanent partnership or reader access. A learning note grants no future real-record permission. Unfinished use leaves operational claims open without erasing the actual revision or intrinsic insight; recognize the gains and appropriate remaining work together.

sorting.heading: Separate closing evidence, next responsibility and enlarged result

items.text: Suri says the draft state no longer appears to approve Agency B’s decision.
Reva says the explanation is distinct from approved results.
Clarify actual help arrangements and decision roles before real use.
Consider actual responsibility for later accuracy and changes.
The course guarantees a permanent agency partnership.
Two comments prove every reader’s successful service access.

lessons.next: Next: Use the job aid for optional practice coordination or private understanding, preserving actual agency responsibilities and information arrangements.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: Suri and Reva recognize accurate contribution and decision distinctions in the whole revision, with help, criteria and needs still absent. Em’s complete closing retains real-use and continuity unknowns rather than certifying a real partnership.
scenario.prompt: How should the collaboration learning close?
options: Certify a permanent successful partnership and universal reader access.
Discard every gain because publication and implementation are unknown.
Recognize the exact contributions and comments, with a fitting next inquiry or private insight and actual unfinished responsibilities open.
responses: The account supplies neither permanence nor reader outcomes.
Unknown operational results do not erase specific learning.
This values the work while keeping its future conditions honest.

lessons.transfer: Privately identify one coordination gain and open responsibility, or retain a meaningful private insight without creating a real agreement or public artifact.

move.control: You can describe actual contributions and preserve continuity as a responsibility question.
move.failure: A useful wording exchange becomes certified partnership success, or unfinished real use erases all learning.
move.next: Privately identify one coordination gain and open responsibility, or retain a meaningful private insight without creating a real agreement or public artifact.

jobAid.title: Coordinate across agencies with responsibilities intact
jobAid.subtitle: Connect a shared reader purpose, distinct contributions, clear status meanings and actual follow-through.
remember: A common purpose or shared document does not merge agency authority, permit all information sharing or complete the work.

sections.heading: Begin with a concrete shared purpose
items: The original explanation turns Agency A’s complete draft state into Agency B’s approval and every question resolved. Suri and Reva have invented contribution roles for request and review words, not real agency mandates.
A shared reader purpose can connect those passages while actual decisions remain separate. Neither a joint page nor distinct roles proves a result or makes coordination impossible.

sections.heading: Map the contribution and its status
items: The whole proposed map gives Suri request words, Reva review words and Em a connection/representation question, with actual acceptance and arrangements open.

Suri’s complete means requested sentences present; Reva’s means ready for wording examination. Use material-specific states rather than interpret either as all-agency approval or a cultural deficiency.

sections.heading: Receive personally learned contribution meanings
items: Mira’s radio-circle named words mean recognizable authorship; Teo’s bicycle bounded check means dependable responsibility. They widen Arden’s status and control judgments.

The full selected-sentence/detail offer distinguishes a contribution from whole-story permission or whole-object checking, asks what fits and remains unaccepted. These accounts predict no agency motives; learning through private reflection remains legitimate.

sections.heading: Retain exact offers and practical questions
items: Suri offers invented request words and Reva review-scope words, with actual decisions, criteria and reader needs absent. Em’s full note retains those contributions and unanswered time, information and publication questions.

A planning note is not accepted capacity, a compulsory memorandum or actual sharing permission. GAO’s documentation concepts retain appropriate scope; real information and resources need their own responsibilities.

sections.heading: Connect without inventing approval
items: A wrongly merges decisions through names; B discards possible connection; C retains explanation scopes and real-use questions. The performed Suri/Reva contributions support the complete four-sentence replacement.

Actual sources, practical arrangements, agency responsibilities and qualifying DHS Equity analysis tools remain. A voluntary planning note replaces none of that work; consultant program leadership supports staff capability without a gate for every collaboration.

sections.heading: Follow through honestly
items: Suri recognizes removed draft-state approval and missing help; Reva recognizes separate scope and missing criteria/needs. Em’s full account retains actual time, decisions, publication, reader experience and continuity as open.

Recognize specific coordination or personal meaning learning without certifying a permanent partnership or inventing maintenance assignments. Native American and Tribal-specific matters go to the appropriate office within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).

sources.title: U.S. Government Accountability Office — Leading practices to enhance and sustain collaboration
sources.note: The 2023 federal guidance connects common outcomes, distinct roles, terminology, relevant participants, resources and appropriate agreements. It informs the original collaboration example without establishing Minnesota mandates, mandatory memoranda or actual information permission.

sources.title: Council of Europe — Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Supports exploring learned meanings, wider interpretations and responses that fit the situation. The contribution examples describe individuals’ purposes, not government-agency profiles; private learning remains worthwhile.

sources.title: DHS — Content and writing guidelines
sources.note: Supports reader purpose, accurate required information, clear terminology and understandable next steps. The original explanation review remains distinct from actual agency services, criteria and decisions.

sources.title: DHS — Equity Policy
sources.note: Keeps actual staff equity work, daily consideration, agency tools and qualifying formal analysis connected with responsibilities. A voluntary joint-information exercise does not replace that work or transfer decisions.
